verdicts.rationale: The introduction states these annotation and engineering burdens and motivates zero-shot capability for rare pathologies and animal data, alongside human correction.
Figure 1 describes all three workflows, 127 supported classes, 3D point prompts, and two branches sharing an encoder.
The architecture and overview explicitly specify the backbone, patch size, inference method, class-index binary output, and positive/negative 3D click inputs.
The paper describes independent branch outputs and click-containing connected-component refinement intended to avoid unexpected modifications.
The data section gives the stated volume count, sources, per-source split, generated labels and supervoxels, and post-processing removal.
Algorithm 2 specifies ViT-H, summed features from three anatomical views, and the stated SLIC parameters; the accompanying text explains interactive-branch knowledge transfer.
The four stages and their oversampling, frozen-encoder, and MAISI augmentation details match the training recipe.
All five averages match Table 1, which lists 14 datasets.
The evaluation explicitly defines one click per sliding-window patch, its local 128-cubic-voxel effect, and sampling from prediction-error regions.
Table 1 explicitly flags this bias and preserves uncertainty about training/test overlap.
The zero-shot section lists these four external datasets with exactly the stated counts, mouse resolution, and organ count.

The authors report superior accuracy and annotation efficiency and describe the supervoxel ablation as demonstrating its importance. The supplied Figure 5 text contains axis descriptions but no numerical curves.
Table 2 confirms both timings and all stated hardware, resampling, class-count, and optimization conditions.
The one-case scores and 100-case WORD tie match Table 3; the accompanying text identifies held-out test evaluation.
The conclusion explicitly identifies modality expansion, improved zero-shot experiences, and clinical-partner validation and integration as future work.
